items.stem: In steady level cruise, how do the four forces acting on an aircraft relate?

options.text: Lift balances weight and thrust balances drag
options.rationale: Correct: in steady level flight the opposing force pairs are in balance.
Thrust opposes drag, not lift; this confuses the force pairs.
Weight always acts; it is balanced by lift, not removed.
Drag acts whenever the vehicle moves through air.

items.explanation: Correct: in steady level flight the opposing force pairs are in balance.

items.stem: Why do engineers favour lightweight high-strength materials in aircraft structures?

options.text: They improve the strength-to-weight ratio, aiding efficiency and payload
options.rationale: Correct: a better strength-to-weight ratio is the key design driver.
Advanced lightweight materials are often more expensive, not cheaper.

options.text: Because weight has no effect on flight
options.rationale: Weight is one of the four forces and strongly affects performance.

options.text: Because heavier materials cannot be machined
options.rationale: Machinability is not the reason; the driver is strength-to-weight.

items.explanation: Correct: a better strength-to-weight ratio is the key design driver.
